item: EVE-F04 root cause found and closed: the six-day refresh outage was CPython's float summation rule, not NBA data. The committed-tree preflight compares regenerated artefacts byte-for-byte, so an interpreter upgrade froze the pipeline. Fixed twice, independently, an hour apart: main@78f513d (session f69a11c4) pinned this artefact's minutes to math.fsum and republished one field; this branch names the rule once in scripts/determinism.py and applies it to all six byte-compared generators.
why: Failing test (run 44469939831 annotation): WorkflowGateTests.test_committed_round_captures_replay_before_the_live_fetch (script='gamebooks_2ecbccfd.py'). Earlier diagnostic run 44467720829 printed the single drifting field: .top8_minutes_shares.2026-11-15:WAS.top8[4].share 0.1088 (committed) vs 0.1087 (runner). Cause: CPython >= 3.12 sums floats with Neumaier compensation (docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.12.html; docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#sum 'Changed in version 3.12'; cpython gh-100425). The 12 Washington rotation minutes sum to 239.99999999999997 left-to-right and to exactly 240.0 compensated, so 26.1/min_total crosses the 0.10875 midpoint and the 4th decimal flips. The runner moved to Python 3.14.4; every artefact in the repo was built by a <= 3.11 fold. Inputs were byte-identical on both machines (sha256 of the four game-book transcripts and the team registry match between this sandbox and the runner, printed in data/rounds/2026-11-19-89e98007/runner_probe.md). Verified on the machine that disagreed: probe runs 44478152590 and 44478784862 replayed the refresh workflow's exact nine-suite loop and all six artefact gates on the runner's own Python 3.14.4 — suites 9/9 rc=0 and gates 6/6 rc=0 with the artefact gate (gamebooks --check) green, which had been red since run 44143781953. Full reports: data/rounds/2026-11-19-89e98007/runner_probe.md. Two things the same reports exposed, both handled: this session's own emulator test asserted a pre-3.12 builtin value and so failed on 3.14 (rewritten to compare the pinned rules only, green under both), and the suite left data/app/minutes_shares.json modified — flag 89E-F-04. Note for the board: session f69a11c4's claim says the runner ran 3.12.3; the runner's own banner printed PY=3.14.4 in two independent runs here, so 3.14.4 is the verified reading.
action_needed: Owner: confirm the fix by reading the next scheduled run (11:15 / 17:15 / 23:15 UTC) on main after this merges, then mark EVE-F04 resolved in data/app/flags_ef6e2e6c.json (not this session's file). Nothing further is required from the data side.

item: One live published artefact still changes value with the interpreter: scripts/capture_round_79341829.py regenerates data/app/minutes_shares.json with teams.2026-11-14:MIA.top8[6].share (Klay Thompson) as 0.0842 instead of the committed 0.0843 on CPython >= 3.12.
why: Reproduced deterministically in this sandbox: PYTHONPATH=<dir with a sitecustomize that installs Neumaier summation> python3 scripts/capture_round_79341829.py leaves exactly one line dirty (git diff: -"share": 0.0843 / +"share": 0.0842); the same run without the shim leaves the tree clean, so the committed file is the pre-3.12 answer. The same divergence was observed from the other side on the runner during probe run 44478152590: after replaying the committed-tree suites, git status showed ' M data/app/minutes_shares.json'. Consequence: the scheduled refresh would commit a silent value change into a file the model and the site read, and no gate would call it out.
action_needed: Owner of scripts/capture_round_79341829.py (arena/915d2e99-nba3, PR #143) or the next integration session: route the two float sums in that script through det.fold/det.dq (scripts/determinism.py). The change is byte-neutral against the committed file because the pin reproduces the pre-3.12 builtins exactly. Alternative: pin the interpreter version in the workflow (see 89E-S-01). Not done in this session: the file is inside another session's claim.

item: Rule decision, now taken: published float aggregates use the correctly-rounded exact sum (math.fsum, via det.sum_). Any future change to that is a republish, not a refactor.
why: Two rules were on the table. The pre-3.12 left-to-right fold is what every committed artefact in this repository was built with; the exact sum is what the official game book prints (12 Washington rotation minutes: 239.99999999999997 folded vs exactly 240.0, and the book's own team total reads 240:00). main@78f513d chose the exact sum and republished one field (.top8_minutes_shares.2026-11-15:WAS.top8[4].share 0.1088 -> 0.1087); this branch adopts the same rule for the rest of the gated chain and measured that it is byte-neutral there (all six --check gates rc=0, tree clean). det.fold stays in the module, documented, so the pre-3.12 number can still be reproduced deliberately.
action_needed: Owner: confirm no further republish is wanted. If a published number that the pick ledger hashed ever moves again, open a new ledger epoch in the same commit rather than letting a generator edit do it — tests/test_determinism_89e98007.py asserts both readings so a silent re-flip fails.

item: A CI test runs a generator in write mode against the repository, so 'the test suite passed' can mean 'the test suite rewrote a committed artefact'.
why: tests/test_finals_1115_settlement.py line 125 invokes scripts/capture_round_79341829.py without --check, which writes data/app/minutes_shares.json in place. On Python 3.11 the write is a no-op byte-for-byte, so the tree stays clean and nobody noticed; on the runner's 3.14 the same test leaves the tree modified (probe run 44478152590 reported ' M data/app/minutes_shares.json'). Because the refresh workflow ends with 'git add -A', a test-induced edit can be swept into a data commit.
action_needed: Owner of tests/test_finals_1115_settlement.py and scripts/capture_round_79341829.py: run the generator into a temp directory (or add --check to the test path) so tests never mutate committed artefacts; optionally have the refresh's commit step refuse to stage paths outside an allowlist. Not done here: both files are inside another session's claim (PR #143).

item: The two CI workflows disagree about the interpreter, and that asymmetry is why the bug hid: pages.yml pins python-version 3.11 (lines 72-74) so every pull-request check was green, while refresh.yml has no setup-python and used the runner default, 3.14.4.
why: A defect that only reproduces on the schedule cannot be reviewed in a PR. Verified in the repo: grep of pages.yml finds actions/setup-python@v5 with 3.11; grep of refresh.yml finds no setup-python at all, so its unit preflight, fetch, gates and rebuild all run on whatever image the runner ships. The in-repo pin in scripts/determinism.py removes the dependence for the six byte-compared generators; the ~40 other files that still call builtins sum()/round() (verify/determinism_89e98007.md) are covered only by a workflow pin.
action_needed: Next integration session: give refresh.yml the same setup-python step pages.yml uses, so schedule and PR CI run the same interpreter. This session could not edit either workflow file (both are inside the concurrent claim PR #143). CR-89E-02.
